Add a CI gate for pull request texts (#268)

Add tools/check-pr-text.py, a gate that checks a pull request
description and its committed squash-message file,
.github/squash/<number>.txt. In both texts it checks review-history
labels, through the label lint loaded by file path, em and en dashes,
-ise spellings whose -ize form is the standard one, and a code fence
that is opened and never closed. In the squash message it also checks
line width, revision ids and a subject that ends with the pull request
number. Fenced code, inline code, URLs and double-quoted text are
exempt from the label, dash and spelling checks; a fence that is never
closed masks the rest of the text and is reported at its opener. The
gate finds the lint and the squash folder from its own path, makes no
git call, and exits 2 on unreadable input or a usage error. Add its
suite, tools/test-check-pr-text.py, and the workflow
.github/workflows/pr-text.yml, which runs the gate on every pull
request with read-only permissions and keeps no credentials after
checkout. tools/ci-status.py does not insist on the new check.

Residuals: a defect in a form the patterns miss, such as an upper-case
revision id or an -ise stem the denylist lacks; a false failure on
honest text, such as a hex run with digits and letters in a squash
message; a message typed into the merge dialog that differs from the
committed file; and a description edited after the last run.
